weightedAverageMaturityDays.rationale: No issuer-published portfolio weighted-average maturity (or residual treaty/trust-asset tenor schedule) for reUSD. Searched: (1) docs.re.xyz products and underwriting pages — qualitative short-tail vs long-tail claim-settlement discussion only, no WAM number; (2) app.re.xyz/metrics — live capital/TVL/price series and onchain token balances, no maturity field; (3) The Network Firm AUP as of 2025-10-31 — cash/MMF/Fireblocks holdings and estimated gross premium receivables by obfuscated deal, no residual maturity schedule for Regulation 114 trust assets or current treaties; (4) PPM Daily Accrual Price / Use of Capital — funding via principal-at-risk notes with a five-year program term (docs state Apr 2 2026–Apr 2 2031) but reUSD is a perpetual NAV/Daily Accrual token with no stated token maturity, and holders have no direct legal claim on §114 trust assets. Cannot dual-source a current WAM without inventing look-through tenors.

creditQuality.basis: Issuer docs describe a diversified catastrophe-lite reinsurance book (comparison page: ~$358M total premium across small-business commercial 41%, commercial auto 28%, workers' compensation 18%, homeowners 12%, personal auto 1%) written by Cover Reinsurance SPC Ltd., a Cayman Class B(iii) CIMA-regulated insurer (SP1). Network Firm AUP (2025-10-31) independently verified existence of signed reinsurance contracts and ~$66.1M estimated gross premium receivables but explicitly did not opine on underwriting performance, claims, or collectability. No public credit ratings of the book or third-party loss-ratio examination were found. Limited grade: structured issuer portfolio description plus external contract-existence anchor; not adequate without independent credit/performance attestation.

seniority.basis: reUSD is the senior token tranche: docs (About reUSD, loss-waterfall order, comparing table) and the PPM both state that liabilities to reUSD holders rank senior in right of payment to reUSDe (mezzanine), with reinsurer equity as junior first-loss. Economic exposure to offchain capital is via unsecured, limited-recourse Principal-at-Risk Notes of Cover Re SP1 that are subordinated to cedent/policyholder claims and give token holders no direct claim on §114 trust assets. Structural seniority among protocol tranches is dual-sourced in legal PPM + product docs, but absolute recovery priority is not senior secured — limited, not strong/adequate.

legalEnforceability.basis: Binding instruments are published: PPM (ppm_v2.pdf), Platform Agreement, and Token Purchase Agreement path (docs legal-structure + disclosure). Token Issuer is Resilience (BVI) Ltd.; Resilience Foundation (Cayman IC-414560) acts as agent; Cover Re SPC Ltd. is the CIMA Class B(iii) reinsurer; Resilience Inv SPC holds segregated portfolios. Tokens are Reg S non-U.S. only with KYC. Dual primary surfaces: legal docs page linking PPM and re.xyz/disclosure entity statements. Private contractual Senior Creditor rights under Platform Agreement — not a public fund share or court-registered security interest — so limited enforceability grade.

valuationCadence.basis: Dual independent pins of daily valuation: (1) About reUSD and comparing pages state onchain price/NAV recalculates daily at UTC 00:00; (2) PPM states Resilience SPC publishes a Daily Accrual Price recalculated at 00:00 UTC daily for issuance/redemption; (3) api.re.xyz/price returns a continuous daily reUSD series through 2026-07-26 (price 1.091317); (4) docs oracles page documents protocol-operated reUSD NAV oracle updated daily and Chainlink Data Stream sourcing that NAV. Network Firm performs daily AUP on offchain balances published via Chainlink (Avalanche re-reserves feed). Daily cadence with independent reserve attestation + live price series supports adequate valuationCadence (not strong: full AUP PDF is point-in-time Oct 2025, not a continuous monthly GAAP examination of NAV liabilities).

maturityAndLiquidity.basis: Liquidity design is dual-sourced (About reUSD + products/res-products + risks): while onchain buffer >1% of supply, instant same-block redemption subject to per-redemption ≤10% of buffer and daily ≤20% of available capacity; 0.06% fee; if buffer <1%, fall back to quarterly queue. Live metrics show Onchain Capital $75.54M vs Offchain Capital $179.15M, so majority of capital is offchain reinsurance collateral with treaty lockup (risks page). No portfolio WAM published (metric unavailable). Limited: documented hybrid liquidity with measurable instant path but material illiquid offchain share and queue risk.

custody.basis: Dual sources: custody-structure docs name Fireblocks MPC for onchain idle capital, deposit smart contracts, and Section 114 trust bank accounts for deployed reinsurance collateral; Network Firm AUP (2025-10-31, AICPA AUP) observed management access to bank/brokerage cash ($55.57M) and MMFs ($4.17M) and queried Fireblocks-controlled addresses for USDC/USDT/USDe/sUSDe and other tokens, totaling $154.62M supporting assets including premium receivables. Chainlink offchain reserves feed is documented as the daily publication path. Named institutional custody + independent observation of balances/ownership supports adequate custody (not strong: §114 trustee bank(s) not itemized per trust in public materials; AUP disclaimer excludes solvency/redeemability opinions).

recovery.basis: Loss absorption order is dual-sourced across About reUSD, loss-waterfall-order, and comparing scenario tables: premiums first, then reinsurer equity (junior, ~$77M as of June 2026 per docs), then reUSDe mezzanine, then reUSD last. PPM contractual subordination aligns token priority. No external guarantee, third-party insurance wrap, or dedicated recovery fund for token holders was found; PAR notes are limited-recourse to SP1 only. Issuer stress model (0.03% impairment at 135% combined ratio) is not an independent recovery mechanism. Limited recovery design: clear internal waterfall, no external backstop.
